area → área, same word with an accent on the first A, which takes the stress.
Esta área é só para funcionários.
This area is for staff only.
tristis (Latin) → triste. Think of a 'tryst' that ended badly and left you SAD.
Ela ficou triste com a notícia.
She was sad about the news.
species → espécie. Portuguese adds an E before S plus consonant, just like Spanish: special → especial.
Que espécie de pássaro é aquele?
What kind of bird is that?
Picture a yellow taxi stuck in traffic: the driver yells "AH, MARELLO!" at a yellow light.
O táxi amarelo parou na esquina.
The yellow taxi stopped at the corner.
"ESKAY, SEHR, what was I saying?" Someone forgets the end of their sentence. Esqueci! = I forgot!
Não esqueça as chaves em casa.
Don't forget the keys at home.
contrary → contrário (-ary becomes -ário, like dictionary → dicionário). Ao contrário = on the contrary.
Ele sempre faz o contrário do que digo.
He always does the opposite of what I say.
cervisia (Latin) gives Spanish cerveza and Portuguese cerveja. At a Brazilian bar, ask for uma cerveja gelada.
Vamos tomar uma cerveja depois do trabalho?
Shall we have a beer after work?
difference → diferença. English -ence often becomes -ença: presence → presença.
Qual é a diferença entre os dois?
What's the difference between the two?
blanc (French) → branco: Portuguese often turns L after a consonant into R (blank → branco).
I prefer white wine with fish.
mandate → mandar. A boss gives a mandate, and you also mandar a message.
Pode me mandar a foto agora?
Can you send me the photo now?
Brazilians say "Saúde!" both when toasting and when someone sneezes: to your HEALTH. Think salute → saúde.
treat → tratar. Tratar de = to deal with; trata-se de = it's about.
O médico vai tratar a sua alergia.
The doctor will treat your allergy.
peril / perilous → perigoso. The -oso ending is the English -ous: famous → famoso.
Esse bairro é perigoso à noite.
This neighborhood is dangerous at night.
intelligent → inteligente, one L only. The final -te sounds like 'chee' in Brazil.
test → teste. Brazil adds a final E, which sounds like 'chee' after T: Internet → 'eenter-NEH-chee'.
Amanhã tenho um teste de inglês.
Tomorrow I have an English test.
A bowl turned upside down looks like half a ball: bowl → bola. Brazil's national obsession is the bola de futebol.
As crianças jogam bola na rua.
The kids play ball in the street.
client → cliente. Works for both sexes: o cliente, a cliente.
The customer asked for the bill.
MAHR (final r like a soft h in Rio)
mare (Latin) → mar, as in maritime and marine. In Rio, the final R often sounds like a breathy H.
A casa fica perto do mar.
The house is near the sea.
dance → dançar. The Ç is just an S sound: dança, dançar.
Do you want to dance with me?
risk → risco. Correr o risco = to run the risk. Initial R is a breathy H.
Não vale a pena correr esse risco.
It's not worth taking that risk.
Think 'intend': to understand what someone intends. Entendeu? = Got it?
Sorry, I didn't understand the question.
accept → aceitar (cc becomes c, -pt becomes -t). Aceita cartão? = Do you take cards?
club → clube, with a final E. A Brazilian clube can be a social club with a pool, not just a nightclub.
Meu pai é sócio do clube.
My dad is a member of the club.
pauvre (French) / poor → pobre. Coitado also works for 'poor thing'.
counsel → conselho. Lh sounds like the 'lli' in million.
Can I give you some advice?
computer → computador. English -er for tools often becomes -dor: elevator → elevador.
entry → entrada. Also the ticket that lets you in and the starter of a meal.
A entrada do museu é grátis hoje.
Admission to the museum is free today.
Janus, the Roman god with two faces, watches from a window: one face inside, one outside. J sounds like the S in 'pleasure'.
Pode abrir a janela, por favor?
Can you open the window, please?
long → longo. A longo prazo = in the long run. For hair or a trip, comprido also works.
Foi um dia longo e cansativo.
It was a long and tiring day.
totally → totalmente. -mente is the -ly ending: totalmente, rapidamente, finalmente.
purpose → propósito. A propósito = by the way, on purpose = de propósito.
to taste / to try on / to prove
prove → provar. You prove a dish by tasting it, and a shirt by trying it on.
Quer provar o bolo de chocolate?
Do you want to taste the chocolate cake?
Closed avÔ = grandfather, open avÓ = grandmother. Think of grandpa's closed mouth and grandma's wide-open laugh.
My grandfather is ninety years old.
ligar = to call, -ção = -tion: a link-ation. Fazer uma ligação = to make a call.
Recebi uma ligação da minha mãe.
I got a call from my mom.
sequence / sequel → seguinte: what follows. No dia seguinte = the next day.
The following day, he came back.
A MINI person: menino is a small boy. Menina is a girl.
O menino está brincando no parque.
The boy is playing in the park.
create → criar. Also to raise children or animals: fui criado em Recife.
Ela quer criar o próprio negócio.
She wants to create her own business.
locate / collocate → colocar: give something a location. Very common in Brazil instead of pôr.
Where can I put the suitcases?
photo → foto. It's feminine because it's short for a fotografia.
chance → chance, same word, but feminine in Portuguese and the CH is a soft sh. Sem chance! = No way!
Me dá mais uma chance, por favor.
Give me one more chance, please.
Vou verificar o horário do voo.
terrible → terrível. English -ble becomes -vel: possible → possível. Double RR is a throaty H.
mount / mountain → monte. Um monte de = a whole pile of, a lot of.
Tenho um monte de coisas para fazer.
I have a ton of things to do.
pedir = to ask. A pedido is what you asked for: your order at the restaurant, PEDDLED to your table.
O garçom anotou o nosso pedido.
A whole CHORUS of babies crying at once: chorar. Ch sounds like English sh.
O bebê começou a chorar de fome.
The baby started crying from hunger.
example → exemplo. Por exemplo = for example.
Can you give me an example?
Rio de Janeiro means 'River of January': explorers mistook the bay for a river.
Nadamos no rio no fim de semana.
We swam in the river on the weekend.
Brazil's famous jeitinho is the clever little way around any problem. Dar um jeito = find a way.
Não tem jeito, vamos ter que esperar.
There's no way around it, we'll have to wait.
initial / initiate → início. Página inicial = home page.
No início, eu não gostava de café.
In the beginning, I didn't like coffee.
enormous → enorme. Drop the -ous and add -e.
television → televisão. -sion becomes -são: vision → visão. Everyday word: a TV ('teh-VEH').
A televisão está ligada o dia todo.
The TV is on all day.
succor (old English, from Latin succurrere) → socorro. Shout "Socorro!" only in a real emergency.
A climber reaches the summit, cima: acima means above. Lá em cima = up there.
Moro no andar acima do seu.
I live on the floor above yours.
"ALL MOSS, so?" A vegan lunch of nothing but greens. Lunch is the big meal of the day in Brazil.
O almoço está pronto na mesa.
Lunch is ready on the table.
card / carton → cartão. -ão makes it bigger, like a stiff card. Cartão de crédito = credit card.
coquina (Latin) gives both kitchen and cozinha. Cozinha brasileira = Brazilian cuisine.
A família se reúne na cozinha.
The family gathers in the kitchen.
Cinderella sat in the ashes: cinza is ash, and the color of ash, gray.
O céu está cinza, vai chover.
The sky is gray, it's going to rain.
price → preço. Qual é o preço? = What's the price?
O preço da gasolina subiu de novo.
The price of gas went up again.
principal → principal, same spelling. Final L sounds like W in Brazil: 'preen-see-POW'.
Qual é a rua principal da cidade?
What's the main street in town?
just → justo: fair. Also tight-fitting: a calça ficou justa.
Não é justo, eu cheguei primeiro!
That's not fair, I got here first!
Cha, chai, chá: tea travelled the world with almost the same name. Chá gelado = iced tea.
Would you like some chamomile tea?
vinum (Latin) → vinho, as in vine and vineyard. Nh sounds like the 'ny' in canyon.
Vamos abrir uma garrafa de vinho.
Let's open a bottle of wine.
relate → relatório: a document that relates what happened. -ório like laboratory → laboratório.
Preciso terminar o relatório até sexta.
I need to finish the report by Friday.
It's not necessary to bring anything.
pair → par. Um par de sapatos = a pair of shoes. Número par = even number.
Comprei um par de tênis novo.
I bought a new pair of sneakers.
Your aunt invites you to TEA: tia sounds like 'chee-ah' in Brazil. Kids also call teachers tia.
marvelous → maravilhoso: -ous becomes -oso again. A Marvel movie that's maravilhoso.
What a wonderful day at the beach!
cellular → celular. Brazilians never say 'telemóvel'; it's always o celular.
My phone is out of battery.
insula (Latin) gave isle, island and ilha. Lh sounds like 'lli' in million.
A SUBmarine coming up to the surface: subir is to go up. Its opposite is descer.
Vamos subir de escada ou de elevador?
Shall we go up by stairs or elevator?
opinion → opinião. -ion becomes -ião: religion → religião. Na minha opinião = in my opinion.
Na minha opinião, o filme é ótimo.
In my opinion, the movie is great.
terminate → terminar. Also to break up: terminar com alguém.
Have you finished the work yet?
fact → fato (Portugal writes facto). De fato = in fact.
É um fato: ninguém gosta de segunda.
It's a fact: nobody likes Mondays.
bracelet goes around the braço. Also brace: you brace yourself with your arms.
I hurt my arm playing volleyball.
sack → saco. Slang: que saco! = what a pain!
Coloca o lixo no saco preto.
Put the trash in the black bag.
memorare (Latin) slowly became lembrar: the M turned into L. Think 'remember' with the re- cut off and the M softened.
se + não = if not. Corre, senão você perde o ônibus: run, if not you'll miss the bus.
Leva o casaco, senão vai passar frio.
Take your coat, otherwise you'll be cold.
series → série. Also a TV show you binge, and a school grade: quinta série.
Qual série você está assistindo agora?
Which series are you watching now?
gelado = ice-cold, -eira = the thing that holds it. The gelato-maker in your kitchen.
joint / join → junto. Junto com = together with. Juntos when you're more than one.
I live together with two friends.
Looks like discuss, but in Brazil it often means to ARGUE angrily. Discutir a relação = to have 'the talk'.
radio → rádio. Initial R is a breathy H, and di sounds like 'jee'.
Meu pai ouve rádio no carro.
My dad listens to the radio in the car.
silence → silêncio. English -ence often becomes -êncio or -ência.
piece → peça. Also a theater play and a spare part: peça de carro.
A piece of the puzzle is missing.
At ESCOLA (school), you choose your seat on day one: escolher. Escolha = a choice.
limpidus (Latin, clear) → limpar. A limpid pool is perfectly clean.
Preciso limpar o meu quarto hoje.
I need to clean my room today.
evitare (Latin) → evitar, as in inevitable: what can't be avoided.
I try to avoid sugar at night.
ver (Latin, spring) → verão, the season that follows. Vernal equinox shares the root. Brazil's verão runs December to March.
No verão, a praia fica lotada.
In summer, the beach gets packed.
levitate / lever → leve: so light it floats. The opposite is pesado.
A mala está leve, posso carregar.
The suitcase is light, I can carry it.
memory → memória. Memória do celular = phone storage.
Minha avó tem uma memória incrível.
My grandmother has an incredible memory.
Azure → azul, the blue of the sky. Final L sounds like W: 'ah-ZOOW'.
O céu está bem azul hoje.
The sky is really blue today.
A cowboy in tight pants: KOW-sah. Brazil uses the singular, a calça, for one pair.
restaurant → restaurante, with a final E. The first R is a breathy H.
This restaurant serves food from Minas Gerais.
common → comum. Em comum = in common.
We have a lot in common.
station → estação: initial S gets an E, -tion becomes -ção. Also the four seasons.
A estação de metrô fica ali.
The subway station is over there.
prepare → preparar. Verbs from English -are often just change to -ar.
I'm going to prepare dinner now.
occupied → ocupado. A busy person is occupied: estou ocupado agora.
durable → duro. Slang: estar duro = to be broke, with no money.
Esse pão está duro como pedra.
This bread is as hard as a rock.
equal → igual. Igualzinho = exactly the same.
Seu tênis é igual ao meu.
Your sneakers are the same as mine.
entire / integer → inteiro. O dia inteiro = the whole day.
Dormi o dia inteiro no domingo.
I slept the whole day on Sunday.
dubious / doubt → dúvida. In class, tenho uma dúvida simply means 'I have a question'.
gelato (Italian) is ice cream; gelo is plain ice. Com gelo? = With ice?
Do you want ice in your soda?
bem (well) + vindo (come): well-come, welcome. Seja bem-vindo! = Welcome!
university → universidade. -ty becomes -dade: city → cidade, quality → qualidade.
She studies at the federal university.
A cop stops you for drinking: he grabs your copo. It's the drinking glass; vidro is the material.
Me dá um copo d'água, por favor.
Give me a glass of water, please.
vermiculus (Latin, little worm): red dye was made from tiny insects, like vermilion.
respond → responder. Responder uma mensagem = to reply to a message.
Ele ainda não respondeu minha mensagem.
He still hasn't answered my message.
park → parque, with -que for the K sound. Parque Ibirapuera is São Paulo's big park.
Vamos correr no parque amanhã cedo?
Shall we run in the park tomorrow morning?
patient → paciente. Both the adjective (calm) and the noun (hospital patient).
quanto (how much) shrunk to quão. Formal; in speech Brazilians prefer como or o quanto.
Você não imagina quão difícil foi.
You can't imagine how hard it was.
art → arte. Final -te sounds like 'chee' in Brazil.
visit → visita. Also the person: temos visita hoje = we have guests today.
A BURROW you dig is a buraco. Brazilian streets are famous for their buracos.
Cuidado com o buraco na calçada!
Watch out for the hole in the sidewalk!
success → sucesso. A song that's a sucesso is a hit.
to take / to grab / to catch
Hang your coat on a PEG: pegar is to grab it. Pegar o ônibus = to catch the bus.
Vou pegar o ônibus das oito.
I'm going to catch the eight o'clock bus.
caminho (road) + -ão (big): the big thing on the road, a truck.
O caminhão bloqueou a rua inteira.
The truck blocked the whole street.
partition / parapet → parede: the wall between rooms. A city or garden wall is muro.
I hung the picture on the wall.
Imagine a slow-moving VAGRANT shuffling: devagar. Devagar e sempre = slow and steady.
Think 'trade': troca is a swap. Trocar = to change or exchange.
A loja aceita troca em até trinta dias.
The store accepts exchanges within thirty days.
Not a ball (that's bola)! In Brazil, bala is hard candy, and also a bullet. Context saves you.
feriae (Latin, holy days) → férias, always plural. Also gives 'fair' and feriado (holiday).
Vou viajar nas férias de julho.
I'm traveling during the July vacation.
stella (Latin) → estrela, with E added before ST: stellar star.
Hoje dá para ver muitas estrelas.
You can see lots of stars tonight.
animal → animal, same spelling. Final L sounds like W. Slang: animal! = awesome!
Qual é o seu animal favorito?
Acho que sim = I think so. It's what you find in your mind. Achei as chaves = I found the keys.
Não acho minha carteira em lugar nenhum.
I can't find my wallet anywhere.
A long-legged PERson's leg. Pernas cruzadas = crossed legs.
sonus (Latin) → som, as in sonic. Also the sound system: liga o som!
edifice → edifício. Prédio is the everyday word in Brazil.
envoy (someone sent) → enviar. More formal than mandar: enviar um e-mail.
Vou enviar o arquivo por e-mail.
I'll send the file by email.
luna (Latin) → lua: Portuguese often drops an N between vowels. Lunar is the English adjective.
A coat in a CASE: casaco. Leva um casaco, vai esfriar!
Leva um casaco, vai esfriar à noite.
Bring a jacket, it'll get cold at night.
começar (to begin) → começo. Do começo = from the start.
Vamos ver o filme desde o começo.
Let's watch the movie from the beginning.
partner → parceiro. Also slang for buddy: e aí, parceiro?
Ele é meu parceiro de negócios.
imagine → imaginar. Imagina! = Don't mention it! (after thanks).
Não consigo imaginar a vida sem música.
I can't imagine life without music.
Not sympathetic! Simpático means friendly and pleasant. 'Sympathetic' is solidário.
color (Latin) shrank to cor. De que cor? = What color?
Qual é a sua cor preferida?
dolce (Italian) → doce. As a noun, um doce is a sweet treat.
leader → líder. Works for both sexes: o líder, a líder.
Ela é a líder da equipe.
omnibus (Latin, for everyone) → ônibus. English cut it to 'bus'; Brazil kept the front. Portugal says autocarro.
O ônibus está atrasado de novo.
objective → objetivo. Qual é o seu objetivo? = What's your goal?
Meu objetivo é falar português fluente.
My goal is to speak fluent Portuguese.
exact + -mente (-ly) = exactly. Isso mesmo also works for 'exactly!'.
É exatamente isso que eu queria.
volare (Latin/Italian) → voar: the L dropped out. Voo = flight.
career → carreira. Originally a racecourse: your career is the race you run.
Ela quer seguir carreira na medicina.
She wants to pursue a career in medicine.
limpid (clear) → limpo. Ficha limpa = clean record.
A casa está limpa e cheirosa.
The house is clean and smells nice.
arbor (Latin) → árvore: arboretum, Arbor Day. B became V.
We planted a tree in the backyard.
Você está preparado para a prova?
Are you prepared for the exam?
to take long / to be late
demur / delay → demorar. Não demora! = Don't take long!
A comida vai demorar meia hora.
The food will take half an hour.
dance → dança. Samba, forró, frevo: Brazil has a dança for every region.
O samba é uma dança brasileira.
faculty → faculdade (-ty → -dade). Fazer faculdade = to go to college.
Ele entrou na faculdade de direito.
image → imagem. English -age often becomes -agem: message → mensagem.
conhecer (to know) → conhecido. As a noun, an acquaintance: é só um conhecido.
Ele é um cantor muito conhecido.
nares (Latin, nostrils) → nariz, as in nasal. The final Z sounds like S.
A CORD being cut with scissors: cortar. Cortar o cabelo = to get a haircut.
I need to get my hair cut.
sobre (over) + viver (live): to live over the danger, survive.
A PRETTY black dress: preto is the everyday word for black in Brazil.
cathedra (Latin) → cadeira: a cathedral is where the bishop's chair stands.
Puxa uma cadeira e senta aqui.
Pull up a chair and sit here.
piscis (Latin) → peixe. Pisces is the fish sign. X sounds like sh.
Hoje tem peixe frito no almoço.
Today there's fried fish for lunch.
calor (Latin) → calorie, the unit of heat. Que calor! = It's so hot!
It's so hot! Turn on the fan.
A partido is a political party, never a fun one (that's festa). Also 'broken': partido ao meio.
Ele não é de nenhum partido.
He doesn't belong to any party.
voar (to fly) → voo. Voo direto = direct flight.
Nosso voo sai às seis da manhã.
Our flight leaves at six in the morning.
control → controlar. Controle remoto = remote control.
FETCH the key, we're closing! Fechado = closed, on every shop door.
Through GRITted teeth, then he bursts out shouting: gritar. Grito = scream.
Não precisa gritar, eu estou ouvindo.
No need to shout, I can hear you.
gato (Spanish) and gato (Portuguese) are the same cat. Slang: que gato! = what a hottie!
O gato dorme no sofá o dia todo.
The cat sleeps on the couch all day.
chanson (French) → canção. Música is the everyday word for a song.
Essa canção me lembra a infância.
This song reminds me of my childhood.
Literally 'interior', but in Brazil o interior is the countryside, anywhere away from the coast or capital.
My grandparents live in the countryside.
style → estilo: E added before ST, -yle becomes -ilo.
Gosto do seu estilo de vestir.
I like your style of dressing.
horologium (Latin) → relógio: the 'ho' fell off. Horology is the study of clocks.
"QUICK, DAHR-ling, take care of the baby!" Always with de: cuidar de alguém. Cuidado! = Careful!
Who's going to take care of the dog?
verdant / verdure → verde. Brazil's flag is verde e amarelo.
forest → floresta: an L sneaked in. Floresta Amazônica = Amazon rainforest.
total → total, same spelling, final L as W. No total = in total.
The total came to a hundred reais.
pons (Latin) → ponte, as in pontoon and pontiff (bridge-builder). Feminine in Portuguese.
A ponte Rio-Niterói é muito longa.
The Rio-Niterói bridge is very long.
director → diretor (Brazil drops the C). Also the school principal.
O diretor chamou os pais na escola.
The principal called the parents to school.
Lying on the beach, you PRAY the sun stays out: praia. Vamos à praia!
Vamos para a praia no sábado?
Shall we go to the beach on Saturday?
lingua (Latin) → língua: linguistics, bilingual. Both the tongue in your mouth and the language.
Eles vão construir um prédio aqui.
They're going to build a building here.
band → banda. Qual é a sua banda favorita?
A banda toca no bar toda sexta.
The band plays at the bar every Friday.
rapid + -mente = rapidly. Initial R is a breathy H.
buscar (to fetch, search) → busca. Fazer uma busca no Google.
A polícia fez uma busca na casa.
ouvir (to hear) → ouvido, the organ you hear with. The outer ear is orelha.
The ROSTrum is where a speaker shows his face to the crowd: rosto. Cara is the casual word.
Lave o rosto com água fria.
Wash your face with cold water.
mudar (to change) → mudança. Also moving house: caminhão de mudança = moving truck.
A mudança é na semana que vem.
epoch → época. Naquela época = back then.
Back then, there were no cell phones.
fountain / font → fonte. Water springs from it, and news comes from a fonte.
Qual é a fonte dessa notícia?
What's the source of this news?
I CAN'T, SAD-o, I'm too tired: cansado. Cansada for a woman.
A university AULA is the lecture hall, like an auditorium; today it means the class itself.
rich → rico. Initial R is a breathy H. Also rich in: rico em ferro.
An alarm sets the day's ACCORD: acordar is to wake up. Acorda! = Wake up!
Acordo às seis todos os dias.
I wake up at six every day.
human → humano. The H is silent. Ser humano = human being.
atrás (behind) → atrasado: left behind. Desculpa, estou atrasado!
agere (Latin) → agir, as in agent and agile. Aja rápido! = Act fast!
Precisamos agir antes que seja tarde.
We need to act before it's too late.
ridere (Latin) → rir: ridiculous, deride. Initial R is a breathy H.
He makes me laugh a lot.
post → posto. Posto de gasolina = gas station, posto de saúde = health clinic.
Vamos parar no posto para abastecer.
Let's stop at the gas station to fill up.
agree → agradar (to please) → agradável: -ble becomes -vel, agreeable.
Not a journal! Um jornal is a newspaper, and the TV news. A diary is diário.
Meu avô lê o jornal todo dia.
My grandfather reads the newspaper every day.
interest → interesse. Careful: interest on a loan is juros, not interesse.
Ele tem muito interesse em história.
He has a lot of interest in history.
guerre (French) / guerrilla → guerra. The double RR is a throaty H.
My grandfather fought in the war.
Ainda não decidi o que vou pedir.
I still haven't decided what to order.
Not quite an expert: esperto is street-smart, quick-witted, sometimes a bit sly.
That kid is way too clever.
class → classe. Classe média = middle class; classe executiva = business class.
casa (house) + -ado: married people set up a house together. Casar = to marry.
Ele é casado e tem dois filhos.
He's married and has two kids.
caro (Italian) means both dear and pricey, exactly like Portuguese. Que caro! = So expensive!
Café com leite sounds like a café LATTE: leite is milk.
Do you want milk in your coffee?
I'm going to the store to buy rice.
gender / genre → gênero. Gêneros alimentícios = foodstuffs.
Que gênero de música você gosta?
What genre of music do you like?
obscure → escuro: hidden in the dark. Escuridão = darkness.
O quarto está escuro, acende a luz.
The room is dark, turn on the light.
disappear → desaparecer. des- = dis-, aparecer = appear.
to lift / to raise / to get up
lever / levitate → levantar. Levantar cedo = to get up early.
Ele levantou a mão para perguntar.
He raised his hand to ask.
crescent / crescendo → crescer: the moon grows bigger. Quando crescer = when I grow up.
Your son has grown a lot!
fames (Latin) → fome, as in famine. Estou com fome = I'm hungry.
serve → servir. Also for clothes: não serve = it doesn't fit.
Esse vestido não serve mais em mim.
This dress doesn't fit me anymore.
result → resultado. Qual foi o resultado do jogo?
Qual foi o resultado do exame?
What was the result of the exam?
dolor (Latin) → dor, as in dolorous. Dor de cabeça = headache.
Not data! A data is a calendar date. Data de nascimento = date of birth. Data in English is dados.
Qual é a data da festa?
What's the date of the party?
A GIRAFFE has a neck as long as a bottle's: garrafa.
I bought a bottle of water.
A round BOWL-shaped cake: bolo. Bolo de cenoura is Brazil's favorite.
Fiz um bolo de cenoura com chocolate.
I made a carrot cake with chocolate.
Essa fazenda é propriedade da família.
Closed 'SEH-jee' = thirst (estou com sede). Open 'SEH-jee' = a company's headquarters. Same spelling!
Me dá água, estou com sede.
sensation → sensação. Tenho a sensação de que... = I have a feeling that...
Tenho a sensação de que vai chover.
I have a feeling it's going to rain.
football → futebol, spelled the way Brazilians say it. In Brazil it always means soccer.
There's soccer on TV on Sunday.
billet → bilhete. In Brazil, mostly a short note: deixei um bilhete na geladeira.
I left a note on the fridge.
cinema → cinema. Masculine, despite the final A.
Vamos ao cinema hoje à noite?
Shall we go to the movies tonight?
vent / ventilate → vento: the wind ventilates the city.
Está ventando muito, cuidado com o vento.
It's very windy, careful with the wind.
taxi → táxi. In Brazil, most people now call a ride through an app instead.
Vamos pegar um táxi até o hotel.
Let's take a taxi to the hotel.
quinta = fifth: counting from Sunday, Thursday is the fifth day. Usually just quinta.
chapeau (French) → chapéu. Ch sounds like sh in both.
Use chapéu para se proteger do sol.
Wear a hat to protect yourself from the sun.
to move / to touch / to stir
MIX the batter: mexer is to stir. Não mexe nisso! = Don't touch that!
Means legal too, but Brazilians use legal all day as 'cool, nice': que legal! = how cool!
How cool! I loved the present.
debt → dever: you must pay what you owe. Dever de casa = homework.
pork → porco. Also an insult for someone messy.
Na fazenda tem galinha e porco.
On the farm there are chickens and a pig.
natural → natural, same spelling. Suco natural = freshly squeezed juice.
I prefer fresh juice, without sugar.
study → estudar: E before ST, -y becomes -ar.
I need to study for the test.
partir (to leave) → partida: the departure. In sport, the match: partida de futebol.
The match ended in a draw.
west → oeste. Faroeste (far west) = a Western movie.
O sol se põe no oeste.
The sun sets in the west.
Say BYE to your shoes at the end of the baile. Baile funk is a Rio party.
Shall we go to the prom?
aero (air) + porto (port): airport, piece by piece.
We arrived at the airport at five.
The MEN TEAR up the papers to hide the lie: mentira. Mentiroso = liar.
Isso é mentira, eu vi tudo!
That's a lie, I saw everything!
Means to present, but also to INTRODUCE someone. 'Introduzir' sounds rude here; it means to insert.
I want to introduce you to my girlfriend.
agradar (to please) → agradecer: to show you're pleased. Obrigado is the thank-you itself.
Quero agradecer a todos pela ajuda.
I want to thank everyone for the help.
en + direção: the direction you're sent in. Brazil says endereço; Portugal says morada.
map → mapa. Masculine despite the -a, like o dia and o problema.
infirmary → enfermeira: she works in the infirmary. Enfermeiro for a man.
A enfermeira mediu a minha pressão.
The nurse took my blood pressure.
visit → visitar. Visitar is for places and people alike.
Quero visitar o Pantanal um dia.
I want to visit the Pantanal one day.
to stand / to bear / to hold on
"AH, GWEN, I can't stand it!" Não aguento mais = I can't take it anymore.
I can't stand this heat anymore.
abrir (to open) → aberto. Shop signs: ABERTO / FECHADO.
A padaria está aberta até as nove.
The bakery is open until nine.
Lares were the Roman household gods guarding the home: lar. Lar, doce lar = home sweet home.
instant → instante. Um instante! = One moment!
Wait a moment, I'll be right back.
Picture a compass: L for leste on the right, O for oeste on the left. Zona Leste is São Paulo's east side.
Ele mora na zona leste da cidade.
He lives on the east side of the city.
used → usado. Carro usado = used car.
family → familiar: almoço familiar = family lunch. Also familiar, as in English.
That face looks familiar to me.
parecer (to seem) → parecido: things that seem the same. Parecido com = similar to.
Você é muito parecido com seu pai.
You look a lot like your dad.
to turn off / to hang up
des- (un-) + ligar (to turn on, to call): to switch off or hang up.
Turn off the light when you leave.
preoccupy → preocupar. Não se preocupe! = Don't worry!
Não se preocupe, vai dar tudo certo.
Don't worry, everything will be fine.
Your PRIME playmate at family gatherings: your primo. Prima for a girl.
PEDAL a bike to the bakery and grab a piece of cake: pedaço.
jardin (French) → jardim. Same root as yard and garden.
My mom takes care of the garden.
secret → segredo: c becomes g, t becomes d. Guarda segredo? = Can you keep a secret?
Can I tell you a secret?
ovum (Latin) → ovo, as in oval and ovulation: egg-shaped.
Quero um ovo frito, por favor.
I'd like a fried egg, please.
Literally 'coffee of the morning'. Portugal says pequeno-almoço; Brazil says café da manhã.
O café da manhã está incluído?
melior (Latin, better) → melhorar, as in ameliorate. Melhoras! = Get well soon!
Your Portuguese has improved a lot!
member → membro. The B moved: memb-ER → memb-RO.
He's a member of the club.
chemise → camisa. Camisa do Brasil = the yellow soccer jersey.
Ele usa camisa social no trabalho.
He wears a dress shirt at work.
voyage → viajar. Boa viagem! = Have a good trip!
somnus (Latin, sleep) → sonho, sonhar: what you do while asleep. Sonhar com = to dream about.
I dreamed about you last night.
utility → útil. Dia útil = business day.
mass → massa. Pasta, dough and cake batter are all massa. Slang: massa! = awesome!
A massa da pizza está pronta.
jamais (French) → jamais. Stronger than nunca: jamais! = never ever!
false → falso. Nota falsa = counterfeit bill.
to win / to beat / to expire
vincere (Latin) → vencer, as in invincible. Also to expire: o leite venceu.
nix, nivis (Latin) → neve. Sierra Nevada = snowy mountain range.
I've never seen snow in my life.
advise / advisory → aviso. Aviso prévio = notice period at work.
There's a notice on the door.
nascent / native → nascer. Nasci em 1990 = I was born in 1990. Nascer do sol = sunrise.
Sabbath → sábado: the day of rest. Brazil's weekdays are numbered, but Saturday kept its name.
On Saturday we're going to the beach.
Say BYE to the city center and head home to your bairro.
complete → completo. Hotel completo = fully booked.
void / vacuum → vazio. Estômago vazio = empty stomach.
companion → companheiro: someone you share bread with. Often a life partner.
Ela foi com o companheiro dela.
quiet → quieto. Fica quieto! = Keep still! / Be quiet!
Fica quieto um minuto, por favor.
Keep still for a minute, please.
discourse → discurso. Fazer um discurso = to give a speech.
O discurso do noivo foi lindo.
chocolate → chocolate, same spelling, but CH = sh and the final -te = 'chee'.
I want a chocolate ice cream.
salary → salário. Roman soldiers were paid in sal (salt): sal → salário.
Recebo o salário no dia cinco.
I get my salary on the fifth.
A tall, proud building on a PRAIRIE: prédio. Everyday word for a block of flats.
Moro no décimo andar do prédio.
I live on the tenth floor of the building.
caçar (to hunt) → caça. Caça ao tesouro = treasure hunt.
As crianças adoram caça ao tesouro.
Not a bolster: bolsa is a handbag. Bolsa de estudos = scholarship; Bolsa de Valores = stock exchange.
I left my purse in the taxi!
amare (Latin) → amar: amorous, amateur (someone who does it for love).
to keep / to put away / to save
guard → guardar: keep it safe. Guardar dinheiro = to save money.
Put the toys away in the box.
mountain → montanha. Montanha-russa (Russian mountain) = roller coaster.
We climbed the mountain on foot.
A FRAgile cup is weak: fraco. Café fraco = weak coffee.
O sinal do wi-fi está fraco.
model → modelo. Works for fashion models and car models alike.
Qual é o modelo do seu celular?
SHOO! the rain away: chuva. Chover = to rain; guarda-chuva = umbrella.
There will be rain in the afternoon.
Ela gosta de ciência e matemática.
panis (Latin) → pão: pantry, companion (bread-sharer). Pão francês = Brazil's daily roll.
I bought warm bread at the bakery.
dentist / dental → dente. Escovar os dentes = to brush your teeth.
Preciso ir ao dentista, meu dente dói.
I need to see the dentist, my tooth hurts.
exam → exame. In Brazil, also a medical test: exame de sangue = blood test.
Amanhã faço um exame de sangue.
Tomorrow I'm getting a blood test.
lavatory / lavender (used in washing) → lavar. Lavar a louça = to do the dishes.
Quem vai lavar a louça hoje?
zero → zero. Zero a zero = nil-nil. Carro zero = brand-new car.
O jogo terminou zero a zero.
The game ended zero to zero.
You SUCK juice through a straw: suco. Portugal says sumo; Brazil says suco.
Um suco de laranja, por favor.
impression → impressão: -ssion becomes -ssão. Also printing: impressora = printer.
I got a good impression of him.
pilot → piloto. Brazil loves its Formula 1 pilotos, like Senna.
principle → princípio. A princípio = at first; em princípio = in principle.
A princípio, achei o curso difícil.
At first, I thought the course was hard.
On the corner, you ESKEE-nah around the turn on your skates. Na esquina = on the corner.
The pharmacy is on the corner.
intention → intenção. -tion becomes -ção. Sem intenção = unintentionally.
Não foi minha intenção te magoar.
It wasn't my intention to hurt you.
course → curso. Curso de inglês = English course; also a college major.
dies Dominicus (Latin, the Lord's day) → domingo. Brazil's day for family lunch.
No domingo, almoçamos na casa da vó.
On Sunday, we have lunch at grandma's.
note → nota. A school grade, a musical note, and a banknote: nota de cem.
I got a ten on the test!
interview → entrevista: entre (inter) + vista (view), piece by piece.
Tenho uma entrevista de emprego hoje.
I have a job interview today.
recent + -mente = recently. Long word, simple rule.
entre (between) + tanto: in between all that. Formal; in speech, Brazilians say mas or só que.
O plano é bom; entretanto, é caro.
The plan is good; however, it's expensive.
caseus (Latin) → queijo, like casein. Pão de queijo is Minas Gerais's famous cheese bread.
to gather / to join / to save up
join / joint → juntar. Juntar dinheiro = to save up money.
comprehend → compreender. A bit more formal than entender.
honest → honesto. The H is silent in both languages.
article → artigo. Also a grammar article: o, a.
I read an interesting article today.
gelato (Italian) → gelado. Brazilians want their beer bem gelada.
Uma cerveja bem gelada, por favor.
extra → extra, same word. The X sounds like S here. Hora extra = overtime.
I did two hours of overtime today.
vicinus (Latin) → vizinho, as in vicinity: the people in your vicinity.
O vizinho de cima é muito barulhento.
The upstairs neighbor is very noisy.
lesson → lição. Lição de casa = homework. Aprendi a lição!
Aprendi a lição: nunca mais faço isso.
I learned my lesson: never doing that again.
People in single FILE: a fila. Brazil has lines for everything, even at the bakery.
A fila do banco está enorme.
The line at the bank is huge.
Vou vestir uma roupa mais leve.
I'm going to put on lighter clothes.
"Garota de Ipanema" (The Girl from Ipanema), the famous bossa nova song.
piscis (Latin, fish) → piscina: originally a fish pond.
The kids are in the pool.
offer → oferecer. Posso te oferecer um café?
Can I offer you a coffee?
insignia / sign → ensinar: to show the signs. Ensinar alguém a fazer algo.
Minha avó me ensinou a cozinhar.
My grandma taught me to cook.
to change / to exchange / to swap
TRUCK-ar your stuff: you load it up and trade it. Trocar de roupa = to change clothes.
diversion → diversão: a fun diversion. Parque de diversões = amusement park.
adore → adorar. Brazilians use it all the time: adorei! = I loved it!
incendiary → incêndio: a fire that destroys. A cooking flame is fogo.
Felicidade é estar com a família.
com (with) + partilhar (to split): to share. Portugal says partilhar; Brazil says compartilhar.
I shared the video in the group.
localization → localização. Manda a localização! = Send me your location!
regula (Latin) → regra, as in regular and regulation.
Em casa, a regra é tirar o sapato.
At home, the rule is to take your shoes off.
minor → menor. Menor de idade = underage.
Meu irmão menor tem dez anos.
veer → virar: veer right. Vira à direita = turn right. Also to become: virou médico.
Turn left at the traffic light.
alcohol → álcool. Also the fuel: Brazilian cars run on álcool (ethanol).
divine → adivinhar: a diviner guesses the future. Adivinha! = Guess what!
Guess who I ran into today!
cartão (card) + -eira: the thing that holds the cards. Carteira de motorista = driver's license.
Perdi a carteira com todos os documentos.
I lost my wallet with all my documents.
telephone → telefonar. In everyday Brazil, ligar is more common.
I'm going to call the doctor.
Esse restaurante é famoso pela feijoada.
This restaurant is famous for its feijoada.
Not to attend! Atender is to answer the phone or serve a customer. To attend is frequentar or assistir.
Pode atender o telefone, por favor?
Can you answer the phone, please?
passage → passagem: -age becomes -agem. The ticket that buys your passage.
I bought the ticket to Recife.
A big GOURD sitting on the table: gordo. Brazilians use it affectionately too.
O gato ficou gordo de tanto comer.
The cat got fat from eating so much.
SIT and get CENTERED: sentar. Senta aqui! = Sit here!
Have a seat, make yourself at home.
rob → roubar. Initial R is a breathy H: 'hoh-BAHR'.
sufficient → suficiente. Já é suficiente, obrigado = That's enough, thanks.
We have enough food for everyone.
A BARGAIN at the market: barato. Opposite of caro.
She has a talent for music.
page → página. The stress is on the first syllable: PAH-zhee-nah.
Abram o livro na página dez.
Open your books to page ten.
identification → identificação. The longest -tion/-ção you'll meet today.
I need to see your ID.
Someone CHATTED behind your back and now you're upset: chateado.
Fiquei chateado com o que ele disse.
I got upset about what he said.
"NO! GENTLE..." you say, backing away from something gross: nojento. Nojo = disgust.
artist → artista. Same form for a man or woman: o artista, a artista.
Ele é um artista de rua.
terrain → terreno. Comprar um terreno = to buy a plot of land.
They bought a plot of land at the beach.
Not only to experiment: it's to try something out. Experimentar uma roupa = to try on clothes.
Can I try on this dress?
permit → permitir. É permitido? = Is it allowed?
"É brincadeira!" = Just kidding! Brincar is what kids do: play.
Relax, it was just a joke!
Two meanings: cantar → canto (singing), and the corner of a room. Fica no canto = stay in the corner.
Coloca a planta no canto da sala.
Put the plant in the corner of the room.
traverse → atravessar. Atravessar a rua = to cross the street.
A witch flying on her BRUSH-broom: bruxa. X sounds like sh.
A bruxa do filme dava medo.
The witch in the movie was scary.
alumnus → aluno: the M fell away. Aluna for a girl.
band (group) → bando. Um bando de = a bunch of.
Um bando de pássaros passou voando.
A flock of birds flew by.
transit → trânsito. São Paulo's trânsito is legendary.
Traffic is at a standstill today.
courier → correio. Correios is Brazil's postal service.
I sent the package by mail.
carry / cargo → carregar. Also to charge your phone: carregar o celular.
I need to charge my phone.
to ruin / to spoil / to break
A STRAY GAR-den hose floods the lawn and ruins it: estragar. Comida estragada = spoiled food.
cair (to fall) → queda. Queda de energia = power outage.
Houve uma queda de energia ontem.
There was a power outage yesterday.
"AH, HOSE down that rice!" Arroz e feijão: rice and beans, the Brazilian everyday plate.
Arroz e feijão todo dia, sem falta.
Rice and beans every day, without fail.
Blow on a dusty shelf: "POH!" Café em pó = ground coffee.
Os móveis estão cheios de pó.
The furniture is covered in dust.
theater → teatro. Brazilian T before 'e' in an unstressed syllable becomes 'chee'.
We're going to the theater on Saturday.
period → período. Período da manhã = morning shift.
I study in the evening shift.
An ENGINE salesman fools you with a bad car: enganar. Me enganei = I was wrong.
plan → planejar. Portugal writes planear; Brazil says planejar.
calm → calmo. Final L sounds like W, so 'KOW-moo'. Calma! = Relax!
Not brave! In Brazil, bravo means angry: minha mãe ficou brava. A cão bravo is a fierce dog.
My mom got mad at me.
augment → aumentar. Aumenta o som! = Turn up the music!
Aumenta o volume, essa música é boa!
Turn up the volume, this song is good!
herb → erva: the H is gone. Erva-mate is the herb for chimarrão.
to remove / to withdraw / to pick up
retire / retract → retirar. Retirar dinheiro = to withdraw money.
Preciso retirar a encomenda no correio.
I need to pick up the package at the post office.
só (only) + -mente: a formal 'only'. In speech, just say só.
promise → promessa. Cumprir a promessa = to keep the promise.
hibernus (Latin) → inverno, as in hibernate: the animals sleep through it.
No inverno, o Sul pode ter geada.
In winter, the South can get frost.
fume → fumaça. Fumar = to smoke; Portugal says fumo, Brazil fumaça.
There's smoke coming out of the kitchen!
A ROSE is pink: rosa means both the flower and the color. Initial R is a breathy H.
Ela pintou o quarto de rosa.
The male partner of garota. Common in São Paulo; menino is everywhere.
O garoto chutou a bola longe.
The boy kicked the ball far.
review → revista: a magazine reviews the news. Also a police search: revista policial.
I read that in a magazine.
rat → rato. Brazilians use it for both rat and mouse. Initial R = breathy H.
I saw a rat in the garage!
opera / opus → obra: a work of art or a construction project. Em obras = under construction.
Vou de bicicleta para o trabalho.
vitrum (Latin) → vidro, as in vitreous. The material only: drinking glass is copo.
Cuidado, a mesa é de vidro.
Careful, the table is made of glass.
saúde (health) + -ável: health-able. Comida saudável = healthy food.
repeat → repetir. Pode repetir? = Can you say that again? Also to take seconds of food.
Can you repeat that more slowly?
contar (to tell) → conto: a story told. Conto de fadas = fairy tale.
Minha avó contava contos de fadas.
My grandmother used to tell fairy tales.
turn → turno: your turn at work, a shift. Segundo turno = runoff election.
Ela trabalha no turno da noite.
cozinha (kitchen) → cozinhar: what you do in the kitchen. Cozinheiro = cook.
nation → nação: -tion becomes -ção, and the T disappears.
O Brasil é uma nação enorme.
Someone CALLED out to him, but he stayed calado, not saying a word. Calar a boca = to shut up.
Por que você está tão calado?
Not a bookstore (that's livraria)! biblio (book) + teca (case): the place to borrow books.
Estudo na biblioteca depois da aula.
I study at the library after class.
estudar (to study) → estudo. Also a studio apartment in some places.
escuro (dark) + -idão (-ness): darkness. Same pattern as solidão = solitude.
vacca (Latin) → vaca, and vaccine: the first vaccine came from cowpox.
A vaca está pastando no campo.
The cow is grazing in the field.
"NADA? Nothing to fear!" you shout, jumping in to swim: nadar.
Do you know how to swim?
jogar (to play) + -dor (-er): player. Jogador de futebol = soccer player.
sport → esporte: E before SP, and the final -te sounds like 'chee'.
Qual é o seu esporte favorito?
gosto (taste) + -oso (-ous): taste-ous. Que gostoso! = So good!
The restaurant has a great reputation.
somnus (Latin) → sono, as in insomnia. Estou com sono = I'm sleepy.
ocean → oceano. Oceano Atlântico, all along Brazil's coast.
A ribbon tied to FIT around a present: fita. Fita adesiva = sticky tape. Bahia's fitinhas are wish ribbons.
I tied a ribbon on the present.
comprar (to buy) → compra. Fazer compras = to go shopping.
motor + -ista: the motor person. Motorista de ônibus = bus driver.
O motorista do ônibus foi gentil.
devolve (to pass back) → devolver. Devolve meu livro! = Give my book back!
Preciso devolver o livro na biblioteca.
I need to return the book to the library.
surface → superfície: super (on top) + face. The stress lands on FEE.
A superfície da mesa está molhada.
point → ponta: the pointy tip. Ponta do nariz = tip of the nose.
O nome dele está na ponta da língua!
His name is on the tip of my tongue!
employed → empregado: the employed one. Emprego = job.
The company has a hundred employees.
jogar (to play) → jogada: one play or move. Que jogada! = What a move!
What an amazing play by the striker!
Ela trabalha numa organização de saúde.
She works at a health organization.
"A SUGAR!" Say it fast with a Brazilian accent and you've got açúcar. Sem açúcar = no sugar.
passer (Latin, sparrow) → pássaro: the passerine birds. Ave is the formal word.
Um pássaro fez ninho na janela.
A bird built a nest on the window.
meia (half) + noite (night): the middle of the night, midnight.
doer (to hurt) → doente: someone things hurt for. Ficar doente = to get sick.
I didn't go to work, I'm sick.
pause → pausa. Fazer uma pausa = to take a break.
Vamos fazer uma pausa para o café.
A TARIFF of chores: every family member pays with a tarefa. Tarefa de casa = homework.
Cada um tem uma tarefa em casa.
Everyone has a chore at home.
soup → sopa. Sopa de legumes = vegetable soup. É sopa! = It's a piece of cake!
Uma sopa quente é ótima no frio.
A hot soup is great in the cold.
A BRIGADE of firefighters builds a shelter: abrigo. Abrigo de animais = animal shelter.
We adopted the dog from a shelter.
telefone + -ema, like problema: masculine despite the -a. Ligação is the everyday word.
I got a strange phone call.
sobre (over, after) + mesa (table): what comes after the meal at the table.
A pig in SOOT-y mud is sujo. The opposite of limpo.
Get those dirty sneakers out of here!
announce → anúncio. Anúncio na TV = TV commercial.
Vi um anúncio de emprego no jornal.
I saw a job ad in the newspaper.
filum (Latin) → fio, as in filament and file (a line). Fio dental = dental floss.
Cuidado com o fio no chão.
Watch out for the wire on the floor.
platter / plate → prato. Prato do dia = dish of the day.
O prato do dia é feijoada.
enganar (to fool) → engano. On the phone: foi engano = wrong number.
Not chatty, and not flat (in Portugal it can be)! In Brazil, chato is boring or annoying. Que chato! = What a drag!
Like 'papa' with a little PIE at the end: papai. Papai Noel = Santa Claus.
subject → sujeito: the grammar subject. Casually, a guy: um sujeito estranho.
Um sujeito estranho perguntou por você.
A strange guy asked for you.
limpo (clean) + -eza (-ness): cleanness. Faxina is the big house cleaning.
Hoje é dia de limpeza geral.
A produção de café caiu este ano.
museum → museu: the -m drops and the ending glides. Museu do Amanhã in Rio.
The museum is closed on Mondays.
race → raça. Also a dog breed: cachorro de raça = purebred dog.
Que raça é o seu cachorro?
declaration → declaração. Declaração de amor = love confession.
Ele fez uma declaração de amor.
He made a declaration of love.
significance → significado: what a word signifies.
Qual é o significado dessa palavra?
What's the meaning of this word?
section → seção. Brazil drops the C that Portugal keeps (secção).
A seção de frutas fica no fundo.
The fruit section is at the back.
gallina (Latin) → galinha: the gallinaceous birds. The live bird; frango is the meat.
amigo (friend) + -dade (-ship): friendship. Amity is the English cousin.
popular → popular, same spelling. Also 'working-class': bairro popular.
Esse cantor é muito popular no Nordeste.
This singer is very popular in the Northeast.
sexta = sixth: Friday is day six counting from Sunday. Sextou! = TGIF!
negative → negativo. Also slang for 'no way': negativo!
O resultado do teste deu negativo.
The test result came back negative.
cover → cobertura. Bolo com cobertura de chocolate; also the top-floor penthouse.
O bolo tem cobertura de chocolate.
A FRYING chicken: frango. On the menu it's always frango; galinha is the live hen.
Frango grelhado com salada, por favor.
fail → falhar. Lh sounds like 'lli' in million.
The engine failed on the climb.
concert → concerto. Usually classical; a pop concert is a show.
Fomos a um concerto de piano.
We went to a piano concert.
privy → privada: the private place. Brazilian word for the toilet itself.
sal (Latin) → sal: salad, salary, saline. Final L sounds like W.
Not cargo (that's carga)! Um cargo is a job title: cargo de gerente = manager position.
Ela assumiu o cargo de diretora.
She took the position of director.
document → documento. Brazilians say documento for any ID: posso ver um documento?
Posso ver um documento com foto?
Can I see a photo ID?
email → e-mail, borrowed whole. Brazilians pronounce it 'ee-MAY-oo'.
I'll send you an email tomorrow.
show → show, borrowed from English. In Brazil, any live gig: show do Caetano. Show de bola! = Awesome!
Vamos ao show do Gilberto Gil?
Shall we go to the Gilberto Gil concert?
"FAH-kah!" A knife chopping down hard on the cutting board.
"FIE! O, how ugly!" says a Shakespeare character: feio. Feia for a woman.
Not to assist! Assistir means to watch: assistir TV. To help is ajudar.
Shall we watch a movie today?
firm → firme. Tudo firme? = Everything good? (casual greeting).
Hold on tight to the rope.
"Bom fim de semana!" "Igualmente!" = Same to you! igual + -mente.
A polícia conseguiu identificar o ladrão.
The police managed to identify the thief.
cobra → cobra: in Portuguese it means ANY snake, not just the cobra. The word came to English from Portuguese.
I saw a snake on the trail!
exercise → exercício. For both the gym and the homework.
Faço exercício três vezes por semana.
I exercise three times a week.
village / villa → vila. In Brazilian cities, a vila is a small residential lane or neighborhood.
Ele cresceu numa vila de pescadores.
He grew up in a fishing village.
fresh → fresco. Peixe fresco = fresh fish. Slang: fresco = fussy, picky.
O peixe aqui é sempre fresco.
The fish here is always fresh.
refection (old English for a meal) → refeição: food that 'refreshes' you.
O almoço é a principal refeição do dia.
Lunch is the main meal of the day.
associate / social → sócio. Sócio do clube = club member.
Ele é meu sócio na empresa.
He's my partner in the company.
A BARREL rolling down the stairs makes a lot of barulho. Barulhento = noisy.
Que barulho é esse lá fora?
A KEBAB skewer snaps in two: quebrar. Quebrou! = It broke!
tint → tinta: color you put on. Both wall paint and pen ink.
A tinta da parede ainda está molhada.
The paint on the wall is still wet.
sub (under) + rir (laugh): a little laugh under the breath. Sorriso = smile.
She smiled when she saw me.
student → estudante. Same form for both sexes: o estudante, a estudante.
caminho (path) → caminhar: to go along the path. Great for a morning stroll.
Gosto de caminhar na orla de manhã.
I like walking along the seafront in the morning.
Ele me deu uma flor no aniversário.
He gave me a flower on my birthday.
A CANE-shaped pen leaning on your notebook: caneta.
Can you lend me a pen?
practice → praticar. Preciso praticar meu português!
I need to practice my Portuguese more.
A Spanish speaker hears 'puppy'; in Brazil cachorro is any dog. Cachorro-quente = hot dog!
My dog loves going for walks.
ruin → ruim: something ruined is bad. Nada mal is 'not bad'.
A SAP-stained shoe after a walk in the woods: sapato. Sapataria = shoe store.
"MA, SAN-dra ate my apple!" Maçã do rosto = cheekbone.
I eat an apple every day.
fruit → fruta. Brazil has frutas you've never heard of: jabuticaba, cupuaçu.
direct → dirigir: to direct a car or a film. Portugal says conduzir; Brazil says dirigir.
Do you know how to drive?
I am going to hate waking up early tomorrow.
A SCOUT listens carefully in the woods: escutar. Escuta! = Listen!
Listen to this song, it's beautiful.
train → trem. Portugal says comboio; Brazil says trem. In Minas, trem also means 'thing'!
O trem para Santos sai às nove.
The train to Santos leaves at nine.
banho (bath) + -eiro: the bath place. Onde fica o banheiro? is a must-know.
traducere (Latin, lead across) → traduzir: you lead words across languages. Tradução = translation.
Pode traduzir essa frase para mim?
Can you translate this sentence for me?
Same spelling as colher (to harvest, 'koh-LYEHR' with closed e)! The noun spoon has an open e.
Me passa uma colher para a sopa.
Pass me a spoon for the soup.
só (only) + letra (letter): only letters, one at a time. Pode soletrar? = Can you spell it?
Can you spell your last name?
idiom → idioma: a full language, not just an expression. Masculine despite the -a.
How many languages do you speak?
